name: Device Automation
summary: Atlas for IoT automation: a device Worker Type that drives outputs (GPIO, PWM, buses, e-paper displays) and turns physical inputs into messages, from a Raspberry Pi hosting the server down to a microcontroller speaking the job protocol, with safe states enforced on the device.
next_action: IOT1 increment 2 (step a): the <atlas:deviceConnector> compiler element, reserved job type, worker-only device kind in the server and atlas worker --connector device, so a BPMN task switches an output on the reference Pi Zero 2 W; in parallel IOT0's threat model, which gates step b (adoption).

slices.title: Decision and threat model
slices.note: The owner accepted option 4 of the Device Workers record on 2026-11-05: a device Worker Type defined as a contract over the existing job protocol, MQTT later. Open: the threat model for physically exposed device credentials, which gates IOT2.

slices.title: Tasks drive a device: Linux outputs end to end
slices.note: Step a of the owner's order (2026-11-05). Increment 1 done on branch claude/focused-gauss-i29wni: connector/device and its catalog — named outputs with safe state, on-duration watchdog, pulse deduplication by job key, the GPIO v2 character-device ABI in pure Go pinned by test, a FakeChip; 98.4% coverage; the opt-in hardware test passed on the reference Pi Zero 2 W (gpiochip0 line 26). Increment 2 next: the <atlas:deviceConnector> compiler element, the reserved job type, the server's worker-only device kind and atlas worker --connector device, with the wiring read on the device; runs with today's worker token scope.

slices.title: Adopt a device in the Console
slices.note: Step b, decided by the owner on 2026-11-05 (pull, not push): a generic image or firmware with the server's address and a single-use enrolment code; the device introduces itself and waits as a pending device; an operator adopts it in the Console, names it and states its wiring, which creates the device Worker; the server issues a device-scoped token bound to that Worker; the device fetches its configuration at start and on change and applies it between jobs; revocation in one action. No SSH from the server.

slices.title: Inputs to messages and the device token scope
slices.note: Step c: edges and debounce on the device, POST /api/v1/messages with timeToLiveMs and a messageId of device id, boot id and counter; the device scope's allowlist of the message names the Worker's inputs declare.

slices.title: E-paper display.show
slices.note: Started ahead of its turn at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, a recorded exception to the limit of two active slices. Driver increment on branch claude/focused-gauss-i29wni: connector/device/epaper drives the Waveshare 2.13inch V2, V3 and V4 panels (register sequences restated from Waveshare's drivers and pinned by test), draws a 250×122 Frame with the Go fonts, and talks to the HAT through the device core's Chip and spidev; an opt-in hardware test (ATLAS_EPAPER_HW=<model>) draws a test picture. On the reference Pi Zero 2 W the V3 sequence drew the test picture and V2 left the panel blank (2026-11-05): the reference panel is waveshare-2in13-v3. Step d of the owner's order for display.show itself. Open: partial refresh, content hash, refresh interval, stale marker, the model's layout and display.show itself.

slices.title: PWM, I2C and 1-Wire
slices.note: pwm.set, i2c.read/i2c.write against configured bus devices, onewire.read (e.g. DS18B20).

slices.title: Microcontroller client and protocol conformance suite
slices.note: Step e: a MicroPython reference client for the Pico W class (the owner has a Pico WH; a Pico 2 W has more memory), adopted like any device; a conformance suite any client can be run against. Settles TLS within the microcontroller's RAM and whether it verifies certificates, and renders text through a bitmap the server prepares on lease.

slices.title: Edge server on a Raspberry Pi
slices.note: Measured sizing of atlas serve and atlas worker on Pi Zero W, Zero 2 W and Pi 5; an example application; the handbook card in both languages.

slices.title: Coupling an edge Atlas with a central Atlas
slices.note: Not a record of its own: process-to-process traffic between Atlas instances is already decided in ADR-0373 (a published, versioned process interface), ADR-0369 (qualified address and envelope), ADR-0372 (delivery to a peer is a Worker job, acknowledged once on the receiver's disk) and ADR-0371 (Proposed: a participant names an interface). All are Not started. IOT7 is the edge case of that work: an Atlas on a device that keeps running while the uplink is down, and whose sends park as visible tokens until the peer answers. What is landed between instances today is design-time and read-only: publishing an application to another server (ADR-0129) and one estate view across nodes (ADR-0402).

slices.title: People acting through a device
slices.note: A display with a button is an approval terminal nobody logged into. Decide with the Identity-aware Execution programme who a button press is attributed to before a device may complete human work.

slices.title: MQTT bridge for off-the-shelf devices
slices.note: Own ADR. Broker QoS acknowledges delivery to the broker, not the effect; a request/response pattern is needed before a job may complete on it.

slices.title: Signed software updates for a fleet
slices.note: Own ADR: worker binaries and firmware updated over the outbound connection, signed and verified on the device before they apply, with a way back when an update fails (an A/B image on a microcontroller); likely on atlas hub's signing.
